title: Cockroach Janta Party's Instagram Blocked for Two Hours on Independence Day, Then Restored
excerpt: Founder Abhijeet Dipke called the takedown an 'attempt to muzzle our voice on Independence Day,' the latest in a series of social media disruptions targeting the viral satirical movement.
body:
• The Cockroach Janta Party's Instagram account, which has over 22 million followers, was briefly blocked on India's 80th Independence Day before being restored approximately two hours later
  • CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke called the incident an "attempt to muzzle our voice on Independence Day" and described those behind it as "bloody cowards"
  • The takedown is the latest in a pattern of social media disruptions targeting the satirical movement, which has previously had its X account withheld and Instagram hacked
  • Delhi High Court had ordered the restoration of CJP's X account in July after the government conceded its security concerns were no longer relevant

Brief Blackout on Independence Day

The Cockroach Janta Party's Instagram account — one of the most-followed political pages in India with over 22 million followers — was blocked for approximately two hours on August 15, India's 80th Independence Day, before being restored, according to multiple Indian news outlets including The Times of India and The Hindu.

https://x.com/PTI_News/status/2088492732167925942

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke condemned the temporary takedown, calling it an "attempt to muzzle our voice on Independence Day." In posts shared on social media after the account was restored, Dipke used the phrase "bloody cowards" to describe whoever was responsible for the disruption.

A Pattern of Disruptions

The brief Independence Day blackout follows a sustained pattern of social media disruptions targeting the CJP since its explosive rise in May 2026. The satirical political movement, born after remarks attributed to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant comparing certain people to "cockroaches" and "parasites," rapidly became one of the largest online political presences in the country.

In May, the CJP's official X account was withheld in India under Section 69(A) of the Information Technology Act, with the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology reportedly acting on Intelligence Bureau inputs citing national security concerns. Dipke's personal Instagram was also allegedly hacked, and the party's backup accounts were taken down.

Legal Victory, Continued Friction

The Delhi High Court intervened in July, ordering the unblocking of CJP's X account after Solicitor General Tushar Mehta told the court that the original concerns — related to potential unrest ahead of NEET exam resits — were "no longer relevant." Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav directed the restoration on July 7.

But the Independence Day incident suggests the friction between the movement and authorities has not fully subsided. The CJP has continued to use its platforms to address youth unemployment, education system failures, and what it frames as government suppression of dissent.

"Crackdown on Cockroach Janta Party. Instagram page hacked. My personal Instagram hacked. Twitter account withheld. Back up account also taken down."

— Abhijeet Dipke, in an earlier post documenting disruptions

A Movement Larger Than Memes

What began as an internet joke has evolved into what observers describe as a significant form of digital dissent. The CJP surpassed both the BJP and Congress in Instagram followers within weeks of its launch, and physical protests at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi have drawn real-world crowds. The movement's tongue-in-cheek membership criteria — including being "chronically online" and having "the ability to rant professionally" — have resonated with young Indians frustrated by unemployment and perceived government indifference.

Dipke, a 30-year-old political communications strategist and Boston University student, has framed each disruption as further evidence of his movement's impact. Delhi Police separately debunked viral death rumors about Dipke in late July, confirming he was "fit, healthy and safe."

The timing of the Independence Day takedown — on a day symbolizing democratic freedoms — added particular resonance to the CJP's complaint. Whether the disruption was an automated enforcement action or a directed intervention remains unclear, as neither Meta nor Indian government authorities have publicly commented on the incident.
nri_angle: Highlights the tension between digital dissent and government control of social media platforms in India, relevant to diaspora observers of Indian democracy.
author: Diaspora Desk
